text:
Incident Bot: ALERT - High tail latency and token generation errors detected on /v1/chat (hosted) — 5xx spike 23:41 UTC. Affected: streaming + function-calling paths. Currently 18% error rate over 5m. Paging eng-oncall.
Maya Patel: I'm onpager. Seeing spikes correlate with a surge from a small set of API keys (abuse? batch job?). Traces show heavy structured-output serialization and tool-calls path.
Liam Chen: I can pick this up. Quick question — do we have a hot flag to disable function/tool-calling at the API gateway level? Would reduce KV/cache pressure.
Maya Patel: We do. Two options: edge feature-flag to reject function_call requests (400) or a gateway-level flow that returns a stubbed response with a warning. Edge flag is faster.
Sophia Rivera: If we disable function calls outright, some customers may get broken experiences. Can we instead rate-limit function-calling requests per-key and reduce structured-output size (truncate) first?
Alex Gomez: Ops Runbot shows 90th p99 latency for /v1/chat/generate with function_call headers at 820ms -> baseline 120ms. CPU on model instances is saturated due to serialization + tool chaining.
Maya Patel: Immediate mitigation plan proposal:
  1) Short term (now): Apply transient global rate-limit on function_call route to 20 rps total and per-key soft quota 5 rps. (We can relax if it stabilizes.)
  2) Toggle edge feature-flag to disable structured output serialization for streaming responses (fallback to plain text). This reduces per-request CPU.
  3) If (1)+(2) insufficient within 5-10m -> flip feature-flag to block function_call outright and return: `{"error":"function calling temporarily disabled due to overload"}` with 503?
Liam Chen: I can push the rate-limit to the gateway now. Running command.
Liam Chen: /deploy gateway-ratelimit --route "/v1/chat" --header "x-redwood-feature:function_call" --limit 20 --burst 40
Liam Chen: (logs) deployed rule id rl-6642, applying.
Ops Runbot: rule rl-6642 applied on all edges in 38s. Active rejects ~0 -> ramping.
Sophia Rivera: I'm going to prepare the feature-flag in LaunchDarkly. Flag name: `redwood.disable_function_calling`. Default = false.
Maya Patel: Let's do a canary: enable for 10% of traffic first (non-enterprise tier) and watch for error rate change.
Alex Gomez: Important: also add emergency quota bump for a few known enterprise keys that rely on function calling for critical workflows. We'll whitelist three keys: key-A, key-B, key-C.
Support Ops: Noted. I'll DM affected customers and create a status incident update if we escalate to full disable.
Sophia Rivera: Canary flip command:
```
ld toggle redwood.disable_function_calling --env prod --pct 10 --segment non-enterprise
```
Sophia Rivera: Canary on 10% now.
Incident Bot: Metric update: error rate down from 18% to 9% within 90s after rate-limit; p99 latency down from 820ms to 430ms. Function-call rejects increased (expected).
Maya Patel: Good direction. Let's hold at 10% for 5m and monitor. Liam, can you confirm logs for any customer critical keys in rejects?
Liam Chen: Scanning rejects... most rejects are from high-volume integration tests. Whitelisted keys (A/B/C) show zero rejects. No enterprise production keys blocked.
Alex Gomez: If we see repeat offenders, we should implement per-key cooldowns + require clients to backoff. Also schedule a temporary increase in batching timeout to allow the KV cache to warm (reduce cold misses).
Sophia Rivera: While canary runs, I'm pushing a fallback for structured output: streaming responses will send minimal JSON instead of full structured schema. LaunchDarkly flag `redwood.minify_structured_output` going to 100% for now.
Maya Patel: Apply minify_structured_output now. Command:
```
ld toggle redwood.minify_structured_output --env prod --on
```
Sophia Rivera: Done.
Incident Bot: update: p99 latency 300ms, error rate 5% after minify flag; overall token generation CPU pressure reduced ~35% (reported by model host metrics).
Support Ops: Starting status update draft: "We're seeing elevated errors in function-calling paths; we've applied temporary rate-limiting and reduced structured output to stabilize service. Function calling may be limited for some traffic. We're monitoring." Shall I post if we flip to full disable?
Maya Patel: Yes, hold off until we decide full disable. Notify if we reach 10% error or latency >600ms again.
Liam Chen: Monitoring shows one problematic API key (id: key-xyz) still spiking after 8m. It's at ~40% of current rejects, ~600 rps. I'm throtting that key to 2 rps.
Liam Chen: /gateway throttle set key key-xyz rate 2
Liam Chen: Applied.
Alex Gomez: Good. Also trigger a temporary quota reduction for anonymous/free-tier keys to 1k tokens/min.
Maya Patel: Agreed. Sophia, can you also flip `redwood.disable_function_calling` to 100% if metrics worsen? Define exact trigger: sustained error rate >=10% for 3m OR p99>700ms for 3m.
Sophia Rivera: Affirmative. I'll set an alert rule and an automated LD rollback window so we can revert in 5 minutes if necessary.
Ops Runbot: Alert set: function_call_path_stability -> threshold error_rate 10% (3m), p99 700ms (3m). Auto action: enable `redwood.disable_function_calling` to 100% + post incident update.
Incident Bot: Metrics at 12:08 UTC: error 3%, p99 280ms. All key throttles applied; structured output minified. System stabilized.
Maya Patel: Great. We'll keep the rate-limits and minified output for now and schedule follow-up: incident postmortem + plan to optimize serialization path and higher isolation for function callers.
Sophia Rivera: Created ticket INF-2917: "Increase isolation for function-calling workload; optimize structured-output serialization; add per-key backpressure" and assigned to eng-runtime.
Support Ops: I'll send a customer note to the top 10 affected accounts summarizing mitigations and ETA for full resolution.
Alex Gomez: Oncall handoff: I'm taking second shift in 30m, will monitor for the next 2 hours. Maya, please attach any traces and policy docs to the ticket.
Maya Patel: Will do. Adding trace links: https://trace.redwood.internal/trace/ab12cd34
Maya Patel: Closing thread for now — leave comments if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
